modules.name: aeroplane-core
modules.purpose: Aeroplane aggregate root: CRUD, total mass, hierarchical component tree with weight roll-up, and assembly of wings + fuselages into a complete AirplaneConfiguration.

business_rules.description: Every new aeroplane is created as a complete versioning node: root_id points at itself and a 'main' BranchModel (is_main=True, created_by='human') is created in the same transaction via a three-step flush that satisfies the circular aeroplanes<->branches FK pair (use_alter=True).
Exactly one branch per lineage may have is_main=True, enforced by the partial unique index uq_branches_one_main_per_root (sqlite_where / postgresql_where).
AirplaneConfiguration export requires total_mass_kg; missing mass raises ValidationError -> HTTP 422 before any conversion runs.
Lazy relations (spares, ted.servo_data) are force-materialised inside the session before schema conversion because FastAPI serialises after get_db() closes.

Component-tree node own weight precedence: weight_override_g -> COTS mass_g x quantity -> CAD shape via material density -> none. Surface print: area_mm2 x print_resolution_mm(default 0.4) x density/1e6 x scale_factor; volume print: volume_mm3 x density/1e6 x scale_factor.

Weight status algebra: leaf = valid if own else invalid; non-leaf = valid when all children valid, partial when mixed, and partial-if-own / invalid-otherwise when all children are invalid. total = own + sum(children totals).
move_node refuses to move a node under its own subtree (ancestor walk _is_descendant). This is the only structural integrity check; there is no cycle detection at read time.
Mass sync after a tree mutation is fire-and-forget: every exception from mass_cg_service.sync_component_tree_to_mass is swallowed with a warning so it never blocks the CRUD operation.
get_aircraft_total_weight_kg returns None for an empty tree so the caller clears the mass calculated_value instead of writing a zero.
construction_part_id snapshots volume_mm3/area_mm2/material_id onto a new node, but only for fields the caller did not explicitly pass (model_dump(exclude_unset=True)).
Transaction boundary is owned by get_db(): commit on success, rollback on exception. Services use flush()/add() but never commit().
Domain exceptions map to HTTP as NotFound->404, Validation->422, Conflict->409, Internal/other->500.
GET /aeroplanes defaults to heads_only=True so immutable version snapshots stay out of the aeroplane picker.

algorithms: component-tree assembly (id-map + parent attach, orphan-tolerant, sorted by sort_index)
post-order weight roll-up with tri-state status (valid/partial/invalid)
recursive descendant check for move-node cycle prevention
numpy -> JSON normalisation for the CAD configuration payload

modules.name: wing-design
modules.purpose: Wings, cross-sections (ribs), spars, trailing-edge devices, servos and turbulators; the WingConfiguration topology bridge; the structural spar sizing/solver pipeline; and the mm<->m conversion boundary.

fields.name: aeroplane_id
fields.type: Integer FK aeroplanes.id ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: dihedral
fields.type: Float (deg) — gh-951, NULL on legacy rows

fields.name: wing_id
fields.type: Integer FK wings.id ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: wing_xsec_id
fields.type: Integer FK wing_xsecs.id UNIQUE ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: wing_xsec_detail_id
fields.type: Integer FK wing_xsec_details.id ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: StationData
fields.type: y_span, y_mm, x_c, center_z, band_lo, band_hi, required_od (all mm)

business_rules.description: N stations describe N-1 segments; ALL segment-scoped data (spars, TED, turbulator, x_sec_type, tip_type, number_interpolation_points) hangs off the INBOARD station. The terminal station carries geometry only — enforced in the schema validator, in WingModel.from_dict, and in the service.

wing_xsec_spares dimensional fields are stored in MILLIMETRES (gh-402) inside an otherwise metre-based DB; the API converts with _convert_spare_to_meters (x0.001) / _convert_spare_to_mm (x1000). spare_vector is dimensionless and is never scaled.
A WingConfiguration built at geometry `scale` reads a DB spar origin as factor = 0.001 * scale (scale=1.0 -> mm->m; scale=1000.0 -> verbatim mm).

Only 'normal'-mode spars carrying BOTH an explicit 3-component spare_origin and spare_vector keep their solved geometry verbatim (gh-1053); every other mode goes through the clear-and-recompute unit-leak guard (gh-352/gh-362).
The terminal rib's dihedral is not encoded in xyz_le (it moves no outboard station), so wing_xsecs.dihedral is persisted explicitly; NULL rows fall back to the geometry-derived value (gh-951).

Spar design formula: M_design = |M(y)| x g_limit x j; erf_W = M_design x 1000 / sigma_allow; outer = chord x (t/c) x packing_factor. Section moduli: rectangular b h^2/6, capped b(H^3-h^3)/(6H), rod d^3/10, tube pi(Da^4-Di^4)/(32 Da). sigma_allow <= 0 raises ValueError.

A computed rear/torsion spar is pulled forward of a control surface: x_c = max(min(requested, hinge - 0.03), 0.05). Applies only to solver-placed spars — a designer may still place a reinforcing spar inside a control surface manually (gh-1059).
The root station is sampled at y_span = 1e-3 rather than 0 because the y=0 slice of a real loft is pinched/zero-thickness and would poison the governing max-moment station (gh-1037 #4).
A tip station whose required OD falls below NEGLIGIBLE_OD_FLOOR_MM = 1.0 produces no spar piece; the region is reported as *_no_spar_from_y instead of a degenerate zero-diameter tube (gh-1076).

Spar utilisation is reported honestly and may exceed 1.0 when no round tube strong enough fits; the infeasibility message names the governing station and suggests a capped/box spar. Never clamped to a fake 1.0 (gh-1037 #3).

Front-spar carry-through is 'continuous' when both halves' root center_z agree within 5 mm, else 'reinforcement+joiner'; a single-half surface (vertical stabiliser, gh-1091) is forced to 'continuous'. Rear spar is 'continuous' or 'bent-pin' based on whether a straight collinear rod stays inside the band.

gh-772 dual-role surfaces (elevon->pitch/roll, flaperon->lift/roll, ruddervator->pitch/yaw) emit TWO AVL CONTROL variables: primary SgnDup=+1 with mix_gain_primary, secondary SgnDup=-1 with mix_gain_secondary and deflection 0. SgnDup is a sign flag, never a differential magnitude.
Control-variable names must be globally unique ([role]axis_wingkey_index) — AVL silently collapses same-named CONTROL variables into a single DOF, so assert_unique_control_names raises on duplicates.

differential_ratio is a post-trim, display-only kinematic and never alters the aero/trim solution. differential_ratio != 1.0 is legal only for {aileron, elevon, flaperon, ruddervator}; mix_gain_secondary != 1.0 only for {elevon, flaperon, ruddervator}.

Turbulator optimiser sweeps xtr over linspace(0.2,0.9,15) and picks the argmin cd at the section (CL, Re); it emits explicit warnings for all-NaN cd, mean analysis_confidence < 0.80, and a boundary optimum instead of failing silently. 3-D roll-up: dCD0 = f x sum(dcd_i S_i)/S_ref with f = 2 for a symmetric wing.
design_model discriminates provenance: 'wc' for wings built from a WingConfiguration (CAD-capable), 'asb' for bare ASB geometry, NULL for legacy rows.
_recompute_spare_vectors degrades silently (warning only) on ImportError (no CadQuery, e.g. linux/aarch64) or FileNotFoundError (missing airfoil .dat).

SectionGeometry has two modes: 'analytic' (default, blends segment airfoils, no solid) and 'solid' (builds the RIGHT-half loft once and slices it). The analytic path exists to avoid the ~13 s WingLoftCreator bottleneck (gh-1046). points_per_edge clamped to [8, 4096].

ASB produces N+1 x_secs for N segments and x_sec[i]'s control surface belongs to segment i-1; the converter overwrites the x_sec-derived control surface with the segment's own TED-derived one, otherwise a phantom TED is recreated on round-trip.

algorithms: mm<->m unit conversion at the converter/service boundary (0.001 / 1000.0)
spar section-modulus sizing and inverse dimension solving (tube/rod/rectangular/capped)
greedy straight-piece spar fit with telescoping split, root-collinearity and bent-pin tests
control-surface role -> AVL control-axis decomposition with uniqueness assertion
xtr sweep drag minimisation and area-weighted 3-D delta-CD0 roll-up
analytic vs solid section-geometry sampling at (y/span, x/c)

modules.name: fuselage-design
modules.purpose: Fuselages and their superellipse cross-sections, the STEP slicing/fitting pipeline, and the split of roles between precise STEP geometry (download, CAD construction) and the simplified xsec model (drag, layout, viewer).

functions.name: fit_symmetric_superellipse
functions.returns: dict{center, a, b, n, success, fun}

fields.name: step_path
fields.type: String (relative to ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIR, Surface STEP, gh-729)

fields.name: aeroplane_id
fields.type: Integer FK aeroplanes.id ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: a
fields.type: Float — Y half-axis (semi-width, m) -> ASB width

fields.name: b
fields.type: Float — Z half-axis (semi-height, m) -> ASB height

fields.name: fuselage_id
fields.type: Integer FK fuselages.id ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: original_tessellation_url
fields.type: str | None (always None — STL export not wired)

business_rules.description: The cross-section shape law is |y/a|^n + |z/b|^n = 1 with a, b as HALF-axes; a maps to ASB FuselageXSec.width (Y, lateral), b to height (Z, vertical) — gh-706 axis convention.

Superellipse fitting forces the centre onto the Z axis and mirrors the (theta, r) samples to enforce left/right symmetry, then minimises radius_loss + 0.01 x length_loss with L-BFGS-B, x0=[1,1,2], bounds a,b>1e-3 and n in [0.5, 8.0].
Superellipse area is computed analytically as 4ab x Gamma(1+1/n)^2 / Gamma(1+2/n); the perimeter is numerically integrated with quad(limit=200).

step_path is the per-geom Surface STEP written at OpenVSP-import time (gh-729); solid_step_path is the sewed/healed closed Solid derived from it (gh-731) and is the input the CAD construction pipeline needs (battery-bay cuts, servo unions, carbon-tube bores). Both are relative to settings.ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIR.

fuselages.symmetric defaults to False (opposite of wings): the main fuselage sits on the symmetry plane and must not be mirrored; the flag exists for paired sub-fuselages (gear struts, fairings, cowlings) that OpenVSP stores only once (gh-715).

Slice upload is sandboxed: the filename is reduced to its basename and the resolved temp path is verified with is_relative_to before writing (path-traversal guard); only .step/.stp are accepted; the temp dir is always removed in finally.
NaN/Inf values coming out of AeroSandbox metrics are replaced with None for JSON safety (GH#301).
create_fuselage raises ConflictError (HTTP 409) on a duplicate name, whereas create_wing raises ValidationError (HTTP 422) for the equivalent case.
update_fuselage is a destructive replace (remove + append a new model), so step_path / solid_step_path absent from the payload are lost.

FuselageConfiguration cannot be built from xsecs (literal TODO); its only factory is from_step_file, which applies MM_TO_M=1e-3 on top of the caller's scale and uses only the first fuselage found in a multi-body STEP.
Solid input is sliced with Workplane.split(keepTop=True); shell input falls back to BRepAlgoAPI_Section (gh-727). The outer contour is chosen as the cluster that encloses the longitudinal axis.

algorithms: symmetric superellipse least-squares fit (radius + perimeter loss, L-BFGS-B)
adaptive x-station selection driven by curvature density
outer-contour selection by longitudinal-axis enclosure
STEP solid/shell slicing with fidelity (volume/area ratio) reporting

modules.name: airfoil-catalog
modules.purpose: Airfoil library (1665 .dat files), geometry ingestion and family classification, precomputed low-Re polars from NeuralFoil across an absolute Re grid, three query-time suitability scoring lenses, and role tagging.

fields.name: airfoil_name
fields.type: String FK airfoils.name UNIQUE INDEXED ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: airfoil_name
fields.type: String FK airfoils.name INDEXED ON DELETE CASCADE

business_rules.description: Two distinct Reynolds concepts must never be conflated: this module is 2D per-airfoil over an absolute Re grid 40k-750k (gh-821), while polar_re_table_service is aircraft-level and uses Re as a speed proxy at the main-wing MAC (gh-493).

.dat parsing is Selig-only: line 1 is skipped as a header, unparseable lines are silently dropped, and the canonical name is the FILE STEM (not the Selig header) to match the CadQuery plugin lookup. Fewer than 3 lines or 3 coordinates raises ValueError.
Directory import is sandboxed to <repo>/components and dedups case-insensitively; a failed row triggers db.rollback() so the loop continues.
AIRFOILS_DIR is absolute and CWD-independent because procedurally generated airfoils written by the OpenVSP importer previously landed outside a CWD-relative read directory and appeared missing.

Family classification order is reflexed -> symmetric -> flat_bottom -> semi_symmetric -> cambered; symmetric MUST precede flat_bottom because a symmetric section also passes the lower-surface linearity test.

Reflex detection (gh-834) uses camber-line SHAPE, not the TE endpoint: Signal A camber(x=0.9)/max_camber < 0.06, Signal B positive quadratic coefficient > 0.015 over x in [0.5,1] with max_camber > 2%. camber_at_te now stores the camber at x=0.9.

NeuralFoil metrics are gated at analysis_confidence >= 0.90; min_analysis_confidence is the minimum over the ATTACHED alpha window (not the whole sweep), falling back to the whole-sweep minimum when the window has fewer than 4 points.
Two NeuralFoil model sizes coexist intentionally: 'xxxlarge' for the backfill, 'large' for the interactive endpoint — documented as 'do NOT collapse'.
Polar interpolation between grid points is linear in ln(Re), matching NeuralFoil's training encoding; out-of-range Re is clamped to the nearest endpoint with re_clamped=True reported to the client.
Query Reynolds number: Re = rho x V x c / mu with rho = 1.225 kg/m3 and mu = 1.81e-5 Pa.s.

score_re_agnostic = weighted sum of min(ld_max/60,1)@0.35, min(cl_max/1.5,1)@0.25, min(bucket/0.8,1)@0.20, clamp(1+stall/0.15)@0.10, min(0.008/cd_min,1)@0.10, renormalised by the weights actually present.
score_mission = re_agnostic x family_bonus(1.0 preferred / 0.7 otherwise) x thickness_match(1.0 in band, else max(0, 1-gap/5)) x cl_bonus((1-w)+w*min(cl_max/1.5,1)).

score_target_cl = Match x Efficiency. cl_star = sqrt(cl0^2 + cd0/k); r = CD(cl_target)/cd0; Match = 1 for r<=1, 1-(r-1)/(r_poor-1) inside tolerance, 0 at r>=r_poor=2.5. A CL_max fallback replaces Match=0 with clamp((cl_max-cl_target)/0.30, 0, 1) so glider min-sink points are not universally zeroed. Efficiency = min(re_cd0_reference/cd0, 1).
The per-Re fleet cd0 reference is the 20th percentile of finite cd0 values across all airfoils at that Re (fallback 0.020) — a robust 'best achievable' rather than the absolute minimum.

Only re_agnostic | mission | target_cl_cruise may be the active_lens; target_cl_best_glide and target_cl_min_sink are display-only so the default ranking is never driven by an engine-out / min-sink contingency point.
Ranking sorts by (confidence tier, -score) so a high-scoring low-confidence airfoil never outranks a trustworthy one.

The score treats section CL as whole-wing CL (ideal elliptic, untwisted), so caveat.ignores_tip_re_clmax_collapse is ALWAYS True; risk is surfaced via tip_re_flag and cl_max_margin (negative = target CL above section CL_max).
tip_re_flag fires when Re_tip < 80 000 (absolute floor) or the root-to-tip Re drop exceeds 50 000.

Role tags are computed at query time from stored geometry + polars — no DB column, no migration, no backfill. Thresholds: LOW_RE_UPPER_BOUND 150k, HIGH_RE_LOWER_BOUND 500k, LOW_RE_CONFIDENCE_GATE 0.85. high_re is explicitly marked approximate because the grid tops at 750k.
AeroSandbox import is guarded: compute_airfoil_low_re returns [] with a warning when the platform lacks it (e.g. linux/aarch64).

algorithms: Selig .dat parsing with file-stem naming and case-insensitive dedup
heuristic airfoil family classifier (two-signal reflex detection, aft lower-surface linearity)
NeuralFoil alpha sweep with confidence gating and windowed confidence minimum
parabolic drag-polar fit CD = cd0 + k(CL-cl0)^2 with validity window
log-linear (ln Re) polar interpolation with grid clamping
three scoring lenses: weighted-sum, multiplicative mission weighting, Match x Efficiency at a target CL
fleet 20th-percentile cd0 reference per Re
query-time role tagging

modules.name: cad-generation
modules.purpose: App-layer CAD orchestration: running CadQuery in an isolated worker process, tessellating wings for the three-cad-viewer, caching and invalidating those tessellations, exporting STEP/STL/IGES/3MF archives, and managing artifact directories under ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIR.

fields.name: aeroplane_id
fields.type: Integer FK aeroplanes.id ON DELETE CASCADE (indexed)

business_rules.description: CAD runs in a ProcessPoolExecutor (max_workers=4, spawn context), never a thread pool: OCCT holds global state (BRepCheck messaging, memory pools, interrupt handlers) and the same intersect().clean() call that takes ~100 ms on the main thread hangs indefinitely in a worker thread.

WingConfiguration cannot cross the process boundary (it holds cq.Vector / OCCT gp_Vec), so the parent ships a pickled AsbWingSchema and the worker rebuilds it with asb_wing_schema_to_wing_config(schema, scale=1000.0). ServoInformation is rebuilt in the worker for the same reason.

The export blueprint is generated in the same $TYPE dialect the GeneralJSONDecoder expects: ConstructionRootNode -> {WingLoftCreator|VaseModeWingCreator} + {exporter}, with file_path './tmp/exports', tolerance 0.1 and angular_tolerance 0.1.

map_exporter_type returns 'ExportTo3MFCreator' but the real class is ExportTo3mfCreator, so every 3MF export fails with AttributeError inside the worker; the existing unit test asserts the wrong spelling and locks the defect in.
ExporterUrlType.AMF exists in the enum but has no entry in map_exporter_type, so an 'amf' request always raises ValidationError (422).

The export worker zips everything in ./tmp/exports into ./tmp/{aeroplane_id}.zip and then unlinks every file in that directory. check_task_available only serialises per aeroplane, so two concurrent exports of different aeroplanes capture and delete each other's files.

Tessellation uses ocp_tessellate directly with params {deviation: 0.1, angular_tolerance: 0.2}, colour #FF8400, alpha 1.0, and wing_scale 1000.0 (metres -> millimetres, matching the STL export frame).
The tessellation worker calls WingLoftCreator._create_shape directly instead of the public create_shape template method, bypassing return_needed_shapes and the log-level save/restore.

geometry_hash = sha256(json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, default=str)).hexdigest()[:16] — 64 bits of a canonical JSON digest; is_hash_current discards a finished background result whose hash no longer matches.

Background re-tessellation debounces 2.0 s with a threading.Timer, cancelling both the pending timer and any in-flight Future for the same (aeroplane, wing) key. It is fully implemented but nothing calls it — the invalidation hook ends with a TODO referencing GH #202.

The multi-component scene bounding box is always degenerate: the worker writes shapes['bb'] with keys xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax/zmin/zmax (ocp_tessellate BoundingBox.to_dict), while _expand_bounding_box requires 'min' and 'max' and returns early otherwise, so combined_bb falls back to {min:[0,0,0], max:[0,0,0]}.

Every artifact path is validated by _ensure_within_base (resolve() then relative_to(base) -> ValidationError on escape); get_file_path additionally rejects symlinks. Template runs live under _template_runs/<id>/ and the previous run is rmtree'd on each new execution.

The CAD router is conditionally mounted — app/main.py includes it only when the import succeeded, which is the platform guard for linux/aarch64 without CadQuery. shutdown_executor runs from the lifespan teardown.
The task registry is parent-process in-memory only (dict + Lock). It does not survive a reload and is not shared across replicas; RUNNING is derived from future.running() on read, never stored.
Tessellation invalidation is wired for wings only (on_wing_changed); there is no on_fuselage_changed, and no producer ever writes a component_type of 'fuselage'.

list_executions scans every aeroplane directory for <plan_id> including the _template_runs prefix, whereas _resolve_execution_dir deliberately skips it — a template run can surface in a plan listing with aeroplane_id '_template_runs'.

algorithms: process-isolated CAD execution (spawn context) to escape OCCT thread-unsafety
canonical-JSON SHA-256 geometry hashing for cache staleness
debounced, cancellable background re-tessellation with stale-result discard
multi-part three-cad-viewer scene assembly with instance-reference rebasing
path-traversal-safe artifact directory resolution

modules.name: cad-designer-topology
modules.purpose: The CadQuery geometry library: frozen aircraft topology classes, the AbstractShapeCreator hierarchy and construction-step tree that turn them into solids, the $TYPE JSON serialisation contract, and the CadQuery monkey-patch plugins. Read-only by project policy, excluded from ruff and SonarCloud.

functions.name: conditional_execute
functions.returns: decorator — runs only when the env var is 1/ON/TRUE/ENABLED

functions.name: fluent_init
functions.returns: the class with a static .init() factory

fields.name: servo
fields.type: Servo | None — backs the read-only length/width/height properties

fields.name: xDir / yDir / zDir
fields.type: list[float] — rows of the rotation matrix

fields.name: euler_xyz
fields.type: list[float] degrees — derived, extrinsic despite the 'XYZ' request

business_rules.description: create_shape is a template method: resolve shapes_of_interest (filling None slots from reversed(input_shapes) — most significant LAST), lower the ROOT logger level to self.loglevel when it is lower than the effective level, call the subclass _create_shape, then restore the level. The logger mutation is process-wide and not thread-safe.
Output-key convention: '<identifier>' for a single shape, '<identifier>.<name>' for named outputs, '<identifier>[i]' for indexed ones. A repeated identifier silently overwrites the earlier shape.

A ConstructionStepNode copies input_shapes, removes keys it just recreated, re-adds its outputs LAST (so positional None slots resolve to the newest shapes), merges outputs into kwargs, then recurses. The ROOT node instead hands every top-level successor an EMPTY input_shapes dict, so positional resolution never crosses top-level branches.

The serialisation marker is '$TYPE' = class __name__, and the decoder resolves it with getattr on the GeneralJSONEncoderDecoder module namespace. That namespace contains only ConstructionRootNode, ConstructionStepNode and everything re-exported by cad_designer.airplane.creator — so a new Creator must be listed in its subpackage __init__.py to be decodable, and renaming or deleting a Creator invalidates every stored plan referencing the old name.

The encoder serialises only public attributes (no leading underscore). Runtime-injected configuration (wing_config, printer_settings, servo_information, engine_information, component_information) is therefore stored as self._private and passed as decoder kwargs at execution time — topology objects never appear inside a plan JSON.

_coerce_params converts JSON strings to the annotated base type, unwrapping NewType/Annotated/confloat and string annotations; a list[...] annotation receiving a bare string is wrapped into a one-element list (the guard against iterating a shape key character by character), and numeric strings are normalised locale-aware ('1.234,56' -> 1234.56).

creator_id may contain {placeholder} tokens that the decoder substitutes from sibling parameter values; unresolved placeholders are left verbatim. The class attribute suggested_creator_id carries the recommended template.

Topology classes use a SECOND, independent serialisation convention with no type marker: __getstate__() -> dict plus a static from_json_dict(data). It covers WingConfiguration, WingSegment, Airfoil, Spare, TrailingEdgeDevice, Turbulator, Servo, CoordinateSystem, AirplaneConfiguration and FuselageConfiguration.

Nine of the 32 $TYPE names referenced by the shipped plan JSONs no longer exist (FullWingLoftShapeCreator, FullFuselageLoftShapeCreator, WingRibCageCreator, ReinforcementPipesCreator, WingOffsetCreator, MirrorShapeCreator, EngineMountPanelShapeCreator, CPACSTrailingEdgeDeviceCreator, CPACSTrailingEdgeDeviceCutOutCreator, CPACSServoCutOutCreator), so wings.root.json, fuselage.root.json and full_wing.json cannot be decoded. Nothing under app/ reads that directory.

The dead perpendicular-spare branch: _set_standard_spare_origin_vector defaults spare_position_factor to 0.25 first, which makes the following 'spare_vector is None and spare_position_factor is not None' test equivalent to 'is None', leaving the elif at line 363 unreachable. cad_designer/CLAUDE.md explicitly says to leave it in place.
get_wing_workplane accepts parameters in {'aerosandbox','relative'} but its ValueError message says "should be 'absolute' or 'relative'" — the message names a value the code never accepts.

AirplaneConfiguration hard-codes _main_wing_index = 0 — the same 'first wing is the main wing' assumption that caused the gh-788 8x reference-area bug, which was fixed only in app/converters/model_schema_converters.py. asb_airplane and airplane_analysis are referenced nowhere in app/, so this is a dormant second ASB path.

ComponentInformation.get_z_axis binds the module-level gp_DZ singleton and calls Rotate on it, which mutates in place and corrupts gp_DX/gp_DY/gp_DZ for every later caller; get_middle_point also subtracts self.length/2 where height/2 reads as intended, and the rotation unit (degrees vs radians) is never stated.
ServoInformation overrides length/width/height as properties backed by self.servo, with setters that are silent no-ops — assignments are swallowed rather than raising.

cq_plugins registers Workplane.fix_shape / offset3D / display / sewAndFix / airfoil / wing_root_segment / wing_segment and Sketch.segmentToEdge. Workplane.scaleXyz is NOT registered — cq_plugins/__init__.py never imports the module and nothing else does; its implementation also has a typo'd parameter y_sacle.

Workplane.display is gated by @conditional_execute('DISPLAY_CONSTRUCTION_STEP'): the body runs only when the env var is 1/ON/TRUE/ENABLED, otherwise it logs a warning and returns self. This is the hook the streaming plan executor toggles to emit SSE shape events.

cad_designer/CLAUDE.md draws the frozen/editable line: aircraft_topology/** and GeneralJSONEncoderDecoder.py are read-only (bugs and Sonar findings are deliberately not fixed), while creator/**, geometry/**, cq_plugins/ and decorators/ are open. Enforcement is by exclusion — sonar.exclusions and ruff extend-exclude both drop cad_designer, leaving ~22k LOC unlinted and unmeasured.

AbstractConstructionStep declares construct(input_shapes, **kwargs) and has no implementers; create_XYZ_ted_sketch is defined but absent from the ted_sketch_creators dispatch dict {middle, top, top_simple}.

Units are millimetres throughout the library, in a wing-local frame with the origin at the root leading edge and z up; app/converters/ is the only place that scales to metres for the DB and AeroSandbox.

algorithms: template-method Creator contract with positional shape-slot resolution
depth-first construction-tree execution over a growing shape registry
polymorphic $TYPE JSON round-trip with annotation-driven, locale-aware coercion
CadQuery monkey-patch plugin registration
env-var-gated conditional execution (@conditional_execute)

modules.name: construction-plans
modules.purpose: Reusable JSON build recipes (templates) and their aeroplane-bound instances (plans), executed against a live aeroplane with artefact capture and SSE streaming; the Creator Catalog that reflects cad_designer metadata into the frontend gallery; and the per-aeroplane construction-part file store.

fields.name: aeroplane_id
fields.type: String FK aeroplanes.id (type mismatch: aeroplanes.id is Integer; no ON DELETE)

business_rules.description: plan_type discriminates a reusable 'template' (aeroplane_id NULL) from a 'plan' bound to one aeroplane. instantiate_template deep-copies the tree into a new row named '<template> — Plan'; to_template does the reverse. There is no back-link and no version chain, so the two rows diverge freely afterwards.

Write-time validation is intentionally minimal: _validate_tree_json only requires '$TYPE' and 'creator_id' at the root. Everything else fails at decode time with ValidationError('Failed to decode construction plan: ...').

_migrate_tree_json silently rewrites a legacy root whose $TYPE is ConstructionStepNode into ConstructionRootNode, drops the 'creator' key, flags the JSON column modified and flushes — on every get_plan read.

Execution is not idempotent: each run creates a new <aeroplane>/<plan_id>/<execution_id> artifact directory. Template runs are the exception — create_template_execution_dir rmtree's the previous run so at most one survives per template.

wing_config is built with wing_model_to_wing_config(wing, scale=1000.0) — the millimetre world. A wing whose conversion raises is dropped from the map with a log warning only; the ExecutionResult does not report the partial aircraft.

_rewrite_export_paths deep-copies the tree and rewrites any relative file_path on the four export Creator types to <artifact_dir>/<file_path>, creating the directory (file_path is a directory for exporters). Both the nested 'creator' form and the flat node form are handled. Without it exports would land in the project root, because the executor no longer chdirs.

Plan execution runs IN-PROCESS — on the request thread for execute_plan and on a daemon thread for execute_plan_streaming — driving the same CadQuery/OCCT stack that cad_service's docstring says must be process-isolated because OCCT is not thread-safe. The two rationales contradict each other.

SSE streaming arms the @conditional_execute-gated Workplane.display plugin by setting the module-global display callback AND the process-global env var DISPLAY_CONSTRUCTION_STEP=1, so every display() call inside a Creator emits an 'event: shape'. Both are process-wide with no lock, so concurrent executions cross-deliver events and can clobber each other's gate.

SSE frames are 'shape' {name, tessellation}, then a single 'complete' {duration_ms, shape_keys, tessellation, artifact_dir, execution_id} or 'error'. The generator drains a queue with timeout=300 s (-> 'Execution timed out') and joins the worker thread with timeout=5 s.

The Creator Catalog reflects over AbstractShapeCreator.__subclasses__() recursively, skipping but still recursing through ConstructionRootNode / ConstructionStepNode / JSONStepNode. Parameters come from inspect.signature minus _INTERNAL_PARAMS; descriptions from the docstring 'Attributes:' block; allowed values from Literal annotations; outputs from the 'Returns:' block; category from the module path.

_type_to_str checks for generic aliases BEFORE __name__ because list[X].__name__ is 'list' and would lose the subscript; it also strips the 'typing.' and 'cad_designer.airplane.types.' prefixes so the frontend shows readable types.

Both execution call sites hard-code servo_information={} and engine_information/component_information=None, so ServoImporterCreator, ComponentImporterCreator and EngineMountShapeCreator can never receive real data through the REST path.
printer_settings is loaded from the first components row with component_type == 'printer_settings' (specs layer_height / wall_thickness / rel_gap_wall_thickness), falling back to 0.24 / 0.42 / 0.075.

Construction-part uploads accept only .step/.stp/.stl up to 50 MB; oversize raises ConflictError with details.reason='file_too_large' as the marker the endpoint maps to HTTP 413. Geometry is extracted from STEP only — STL yields NULL geometry because a triangle soup gives no watertight volume.

Every part read is aeroplane-scoped through _get_part_or_404 so a part id belonging to another aeroplane cannot be reached by guessing. delete_part refuses a locked part with ConflictError and unlinks the file BEFORE get_db() commits — the trade-off is documented in a comment.

Part files are stored under the CWD-relative tmp/construction_parts/, not under ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIR like every other artefact; STL regenerated from STEP is written to a tempfile.mkstemp path that is served and never cleaned up.
list_creators returns an empty list when cad_designer cannot be imported — the linux/aarch64 platform guard for the gallery endpoint.

business_rules.description: The critical import sequence is clear -> read -> (legacy) set unit -> update: skipping ClearVSPModel makes ReadVSPFile MERGE into whatever model is already loaded in the native OpenVSP session.

OpenVSP 3.50 removed both the vehicle-level LengthUnit parm and SetLengthUnit, so the importer treats stored values as already-metric and calls SetLengthUnit only behind a hasattr guard. FindParm returns an empty string (and prints to stderr) rather than raising when a parm is absent.

GetGeomTypeName returns Title-Case display names while AddGeom / GetGeomTypes use UPPERCASE tokens; _DISPLAY_TO_CANONICAL normalises 16 known names and falls back to .upper(). Verified against OpenVSP 3.50.4.

Module-level state survives uvicorn --reload: the adapter memo (_cached_module, _import_attempted, _import_error), the importer registry (_handlers_loaded, _HANDLERS, _POST_PASSES), and the openvsp SWIG module's own native VSP model. The process must be restarted after changing importer code.

openvsp_ss_control.register() is never called in production — _ensure_handlers_loaded imports only the wing, fuselage, blank and custom handlers, and the sole caller of register() is app/tests/test_openvsp_ss_control.py. The gh-644 SS_CONTROL -> TrailingEdgeDevice post-pass therefore never runs and imported aircraft arrive without control surfaces, while the unit tests still pass.

openvsp_validation.validate_geometry (gh-647 span/area/MAC/fuselage-length cross-check at DEFAULT_REL_TOL = 0.01) is referenced only from its own test file; the wiring shown in its module docstring does not exist in the import flow.

Wing planform accumulation: cum_x += Span*tan(Lambda_LE); cum_y += Span*cos(cum_dihedral); cum_z += Span*sin(cum_dihedral). The cos/sin form replaced a small-angle 'cum_y += span' shortcut that visibly broke winglets and V-tails above ~5 degrees (gh-755).

Sweep reference conversion: tan(Lambda_to) = tan(Lambda_from) - (xref_to - xref_from)*(c_root - c_tip)/span, returning Lambda_from unchanged when span <= 0. Sweep is absolute per section in VSP — no flag and no accumulation.

RelativeDihedralFlag / RelativeTwistFlag decide whether the per-section Dihedral and Twist parms accumulate (relative, matching VSP's GetSumDihedral) or replace the carried value (absolute). Ignoring them collapsed chained dihedral to flat on Section 2+ before gh-755.

Root_Chord <= 0 warns and defaults to 1.0 m; Span <= 0 warns, marks the geom lossy and skips the section; the terminal x-section is written with x_sec_type None so AsbWingSchema.validate_last_xsec_has_no_segment_details passes.

Airfoil resolution never raises: NACA 4/4-mod/5/5-mod get exact analytic .dat files; 6-series and 16-series get an a-family mean line plus a 4-digit thickness approximation with an explicit info warning that t/c and design Cl are exact but the thickness shape is not conformal-mapped; file airfoils are exported verbatim; CST and unknown shapes fall back to a sampled Selig export; the last resort is ./components/airfoils/naca0012.dat.

Generated .dat files are de-duplicated on consecutive points (tol 1e-9) before writing — the gh-789 fix for AeroSandbox repanel()'s duplicate-point crash — and skipped entirely when the content hash matches an existing file.

SS_CONTROL chord fractions are inverted on import because OpenVSP measures Length_C_* from the trailing edge while the schema measures rel_chord_* from the leading edge: rel_chord = 1 - Length_C. EtaFlag selects EtaStart/EtaEnd over UStart/UEnd, LE_Flag surfaces an info warning and skips, and a second SS_CONTROL landing on the same segment is rejected with a warning.

Source-unit detection (gh-808): OpenVSP 3.50 stores no unit, but its STEP export is metric. Export the largest-X-span fuselage, measure bbox.xlen/1000 (OCC normalises STEP to mm), divide by the raw handler span, and snap the ratio to a known unit within +/-2 %. A non-metre hit converts the WHOLE aeroplane to metres before any target-span rescale.

target_span_m and scale_factor are mutually exclusive; scale_factor must lie in (0.001, 10.0) and target_span_m in (0.1, 50.0) m. Scaling touches wing xyz_le and chord, aeroplane xyz_ref and weight-item positions — never twist, never masses. An info warning always states that masses were left untouched.
Fuselage xsecs are scaled LAST, in _persist_aeroplane, because the slicer refinement must run in the unscaled STEP frame (gh-765).

Slicer refinement gates: only X-dominant fuselages (extent_x >= 1.2*extent_y and >= 1.2*extent_z, measured on HANDLER xsecs rather than the STEP bbox, because a symmetric geom's STEP holds both halves); station budget min(80, max(15, n + 5(n-1))); and the result is rejected unless 0.5 <= x_span(refined)/x_span(handler) <= 2.0 (gh-803).

The xsec slicer prefers the SURFACE STEP over the sewn solid: the gh-731 solid carries internal seam faces at sharply curved loft regions that fragment a section cut, drifting the fitted centre (gh-812; open bug #814).

Sewing runs BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing at a tight 1 mm tolerance and retries at 5 mm only when no shells come out; then ShapeFix_Solid behind a BRepCheck gate, reversing when the volume is negative. Beyond 5 mm the nose cap risks stitching to the tail, so failure nulls solid_step_path instead.

Nothing aborts an import except ImportError (openvsp missing), FileNotFoundError and ScaleValidationError. Handler failures, post-pass failures, per-record persistence failures, undetectable units, unavailable or rejected slicer output and failed sewing all degrade into warnings surfaced by the frontend banner (gh-648).

The SSE stream emits 'progress' {step, pct, detail} at parsing 5 / parsing 15 / units 16 / scaling 18 / persistence / finalising 95, then one 'complete' or 'error'. ProgressCallback is called synchronously from the import thread and hopped onto the event loop with loop.call_soon_threadsafe; the response sets X-Accel-Buffering: no so nginx does not buffer.

STEP export forces STEPSettings.LenUnit to LEN_M before vsp.ExportFile(target, SET_USER=3, EXPORT_STEP), writes under openvsp_imports/<aeroplane_uuid>/, and sanitises filenames with [^A-Za-z0-9._-]+ truncated to 64 characters.

The VSPAERO cross-validation benchmark found five real defects. F1 (#788, s_ref taken from wings[0] making every coefficient ~8x wrong on a tail-first import) and F2 (#789, duplicate .dat points crashing ASB repanel) are fixed in the current code; #790 is closed; #791 (airfoil camber loss, C_L0 offset ~0.43 on DG-101G) and #792 (xsec augmentation makes ASB VLM intractable, 215 s per solve) remain open.
Out of scope by design (RC-scaling focus): propulsion, inertia, CSGroup gain matrices, leading-edge devices, role inference (every imported TED gets role OTHER), and VSPAERO validation.

cumulative wing planform reconstruction with relative/absolute dihedral and twist
sweep reference-frame conversion between chord fractions
analytic NACA 4/5-digit generation plus a-family mean-line approximation for 6/16-series

STEP-export-based source length-unit inference by extent ratio snapping
anchor-driven adaptive fuselage slicing with frame-consistency rejection

business_rules.description: gh-924 single source of truth: cd0 is the PARASITE drag, computed as CD_total - CL^2/(pi*AR*e) at the cruise point; publishing AeroBuildup's total CD as CD0 double-counts induced drag and collapses (L/D)max (17 instead of 24 on a high-AR glider). Every downstream consumer reads assumption_computation_context, never re-derives.

(L/D)max is published from the self-consistent parabolic scalars E_max = 0.5*sqrt(pi*AR*e/CD0) and CL@E_max = sqrt(CD0*pi*AR*e) (Scholz eq. 5.39), NOT from the flattened-sweep argmax which mixes Reynolds bands and lands on a spurious high-CL sample.

Oswald provenance chain aerobuildup_trefftz -> fit -> fallback(0.8): e = CL^2/(pi*AR*CDi) at the (L/D)max sample using AeroBuildup's own D_induced, which costs zero extra solver calls; sanity clip 0 < e <= 1.10.

The parabolic polar fit has six rejection gates and NEVER loosens a threshold: only insufficient_points and non_monotonic_polar trigger auto-refinement (alpha step halved, margin x1.5, max 2 retries). Only category=='design' rejections are surfaced to the user.

Reference geometry is overridden from the MAIN wing (largest planform area) before any run; ASB defaults reference to wings[0], which may be a tail for a tail-first import and makes every coefficient ~8x wrong (gh-788 / benchmark finding F1).

AeroSandbox is the default solver everywhere; AVL is only reached via an explicit analysis_tool=avl, solver='avl', or the dedicated AVL trim endpoint. AVL rejects array-valued alpha/beta, so all sweeps are AeroBuildup.

gh-577 trim consistency: a stored OP is loaded only when it belongs to the requested aircraft AND has status TRIMMED; alpha/beta are converted radians->degrees; a non-empty control_deflections override wins over the trim solver's controls, but an EMPTY override falls through so it cannot erase a fresh trim.
validate_deflections_against_airplane exists because asb Airplane.with_control_deflections SILENTLY drops unknown keys - a renamed surface would run clean while the UI labelled the plot 'trimmed'.

Invalidation: geometry writes on WingModel/WingXSecModel/FuselageModel mark stability_results DIRTY, avl_geometry_files dirty, all OPs DIRTY and publish GeometryChanged. cg_x, cd0 and cl_max are excluded from the recompute trigger set to break the recompute -> AssumptionChanged(cg_x) -> recompute loop.

The background retrim owns its own SessionLocal (it runs outside a request) and distinguishes solver failure (NOT_TRIMMED) from data corruption (INVALID, gh-623 - retrying cannot fix a NULL NOT-NULL column). No pitch-role TED means every OP stays DIRTY forever.

VLM strip forces are inviscid: cdv, cm_c/4 and cm_LE are emitted as 0.0 and C.P.x/c as a constant 0.25. Spanwise panels are distributed proportionally to segment span (40 per half, >=2 per segment) so a 5 cm segment is not resolved as finely as a 95 cm one (gh-855/857).

OPEN BUG gh-955: deflection limits are keyed by the raw DB TED name while trimmed controls carry gh-772 mixing names ([ruddervator]pitch_htail_1). On dual-role aircraft the lookup misses, authority is measured against a hard-coded +/-25 deg, and a phantom 0-deg surface is reported. stability_service._find_trim_elevator (substring 'elevator') never matches a mixing name either.

stability_service._auto_populate_cd0 writes the TOTAL CD into the cd0 assumption with source 'stability_analysis' - the exact quantity gh-924 removed from the authoritative path. It runs on a different trigger, so cd0 can flip between parasite and total between recomputes.

min_static_margin / max_static_margin are queried by _get_margin_bounds but are not in VALID_PARAMETERS/PARAMETER_DEFAULTS, so they are never seeded and the 5%/25% CG-range defaults are effectively hard-coded.

Re-table lookups: cd0 interpolates LINEARLY IN 1/sqrt(Re) (Blasius/Schlichting cf ~ Re^-0.5) and clamps with a warning outside the table; e_oswald is the constant mean of non-fallback rows (Hepperle/Drela: e is Re-insensitive subsonically). gh-924 backfills fallback rows with the authoritative cruise cd0 and Trefftz e.
V_md and V_min_sink are clamped to V_stall (gh-683): the closed-form optimum CL can exceed CL_max on high-AR/draggy polars and back-solve a physically unreachable sub-stall speed.

Vectorised sweeps (gh-690): the coarse alpha sweep, the fine V x alpha grid and the CL_alpha regression each issue ONE AeroBuildup.run over an array-shaped OperatingPoint (was ~150 calls per polar configuration). meshgrid indexing='xy' gives V-outer/alpha-inner ravel order, which downstream consumers index against.
CL_alpha is accepted only when the OLS fit over alpha in [-2, +6] deg reaches R^2 >= 0.995 and CL_alpha > 0; otherwise (None, None) and the gust computation falls back to Helmbold-Diederich.

algorithms: solver dispatch over AeroBuildup / VortexLatticeMethod / AVL into one AnalysisModel envelope
characteristic-point extraction with sign-change interpolation (CD at CL=0, trim at Cm=0) and a two-condition stall detector

parabolic drag-polar OLS fit with six rejection gates and resolution-only auto-refinement
Oswald factor from AeroBuildup Trefftz induced drag at the (L/D)max sample

business_rules.description: Project rule: prefer AeroSandbox. AVL is reachable only via an explicit analysis_tool=avl, solver='avl' or the dedicated AVL trim endpoint; alpha/simple sweeps, streamlines, the assumption recompute and OP generation are hard-wired to AeroBuildup/VLM.

AVL's genuine advantages, as encoded here: native indirect constraints (trim), per-section CDCL viscous polars, and the lateral-directional axis of mixed surfaces - compute_enrichment explicitly warns that an AeroBuildup trim solved only the symmetric axis.
The AVL binary comes from the avl_binary wheel (avl_path()); fallbacks are shutil.which('avl') then the bare string 'avl'. The import is guarded so a missing wheel does not break module import.

gh-588: the NACA regex must match INTEGER digit groups only (^naca\s*(\d{4,5})$). The earlier decimal-tolerant pattern routed 'naca23013.5' into an AvlNaca and crashed AVL with 'Read error on line N'; decimal names are custom .dat files and must go through AFIL.

Control-variable names must be globally unique: AVL silently collapses same-named CONTROL variables into one DOF (avl_doc 778-789). Names are deduped PER SURFACE first (panel duplication legitimately repeats a name within a surface) and then asserted unique across surfaces.

gh-772: a dual-role surface (elevon/flaperon/ruddervator) emits TWO CONTROL variables on the same section - primary symmetric SgnDup=+1 and secondary antisymmetric SgnDup=-1 - so the trimmer drives each axis independently. The secondary axis carries deflection=0 so the single-axis AeroBuildup fallback never receives a roll/yaw deflection.
CONTROL blocks are duplicated onto sections i and i+1 so AVL interpolates the deflection across the panel strip, mirroring the AeroSandbox representation.

gh-590 spacing rule: n_span must be at least ceil(span/min_gap)+2 or AVL aborts with 'Cannot adjust spanwise spacing at section N'. Coincident sections (gap <= 1e-9) are excluded from min_gap so a chord/twist discontinuity cannot force n_span to infinity.

Unswept wings (< 5 deg) without a centreline break switch to s_space = -2.0 (-sine), concentrating panels at root and tip where the induced-drag gradient is steepest; control surfaces raise n_chord to at least 16 for hinge-line resolution.

CDCL injection preserves any section whose CDCL is present and not all-zero (user-edited values win) and caches NeuralFoil polars on hashable primitives only (lru_cache 128). NaN/Inf from NeuralFoil degrade to an all-zero CDCL with a warning. A surface/wing count mismatch only warns and truncates.

build_control_deflection_commands replaces AeroSandbox's hard-coded 'd1 d1 1': it keeps the first occurrence of each name and emits d{i} d{i} {deflection} in the SAME order that get_control_surface_index_map assigns indices, so the two can never drift. Symmetric pairs share one ASB name and collapse to one AVL d-index (gh-529 YDUPLICATE dedup).

A non-zero AVL return code is only logged; a missing output.txt raises FileNotFoundError with the first 500 chars of stdout; a timeout kills the process and raises RuntimeError. AVL routinely exits non-zero, so leniency is deliberate.

AVL results are post-processed exactly like the old asb.AVL.run(): lowercase Alpha/Beta/Mach, strip the 'tot' suffix, redimensionalise rates, compute L/Y/D and l_b/m_b/n_b, the spiral parameter Clb*Cnr/(Clr*Cnb), and the wind/body/geometry force and moment vectors.
AVL trim convergence is INFERRED from the presence of 'CL' in the raw result dict, not from an AVL convergence flag.

gh-529 replay safety: the artefact geometry hash covers only wing/xsec order and (name, symmetric, hinge_point) per control surface - coordinates are deliberately excluded because they are irrelevant to indexing and drift on every edit. A non-None AvlReplayMismatch must be treated as a hard failure.

The stored .avl file is honoured only when is_user_edited AND NOT is_dirty. Geometry writes set is_dirty via the same listeners that mark OPs dirty; nothing ever clears it except a user PUT or a regenerate (which deletes the row).
Fuselages never reach AVL: AvlBody/BFIL is implemented but no code path constructs one, so every AVL run is wing-only while AeroBuildup does model the fuselage.

update_assumption fires AssumptionChanged (and marks OPs dirty for mass/cg_x) ONLY when active_source == ESTIMATE - editing an estimate while the calculated value is active does not change the effective value, so the retrim chain must not fire. switch_source always fires and schedules a recompute for every param except cg_x (the recompute's own output).

Changing mission_type rewrites design_assumptions.estimate_value from the preset's suggested_estimates but NEVER touches calculated_value / calculated_source / active_source, which stay owned by assumption_compute_service. An unknown mission_type is a silent no-op.

gh-526: per-configuration stall speeds come from physics (one AeroBuildup pass per high-lift configuration, V_s = sqrt(2mg/(rho*S*CL_max_cfg))). The historical 0.95 / 0.90 V_s multipliers are deliberately NOT applied when only a legacy clean v_stall_mps is cached (audit 5.5); a cold start stamps STALE_NO_POLAR on every generated OP.

gh-527/536: flap targets are clipped to the MOST RESTRICTIVE flap-role TED limit (min across all flap TEDs) with a FLAP_DEFLECTION_CLIPPED warning. With no flap-role TED no limit is manufactured. AVL has no internal hinge clamp and NeuralFoil silently extrapolates tau(x_h/c) past its training range.
Targets whose required control axes are absent are SKIPPED, not failed: turn_* needs roll OR yaw, dutch_role_start needs yaw, stall_with_flaps needs a flap.

Two-stage trim: asb.Opti (max_iter 120, max_runtime 0.35 s, behavior_on_failure='return_last') minimising 50*Cm^2 + 3*CY^2 [+15*(CL-CL_target)^2] [+2*Cl^2+2*Cn^2 for turns] + 0.001*sum(delta^2); if trim_score >= 0.35 a grid search over velocity factors x alpha x beta takes over and updates alpha AND velocity (gh-528). trim_method carries the solver-path label because trim_residuals is typed dict[str, float] and Pydantic rejects strings (gh-627).
A turn target is marked LIMIT_REACHED with STALL_IN_TURN when V < V_s1*sqrt(n), n = 1/cos(bank) - otherwise the trimmer silently returns a solution at the wrong load factor.

gh-867: the streaming OP generation runs on a bounded spawn ProcessPool (max(1, min(4, cpu-1)) workers, BLAS pinned to one thread) because the CasADi/IPOPT solve does not release the GIL - threads benchmarked at 0.35-0.89x, processes at ~2.9x. Workers never touch the database; the main thread owns persistence and commits each OP as it completes. The batch path stays sequential on purpose.

Gust envelope uses the MEAN GEOMETRIC chord c_bar = S_ref/b_ref, not the MAC: mu_g = 2*(W/S)/(rho*c_bar*CL_alpha*g), K_g = 0.88*mu_g/(5.3+mu_g), dn = 0.5*rho*V*CL_alpha*U*K_g/(W/S), with U = 15.24 m/s below V_C tapering to 7.62 m/s at V_D (Pratt-Walker NACA TN 2964 / FAR-25.341 / CS-VLA.333).
The CL_alpha fallback is Helmbold-Diederich 2*pi*AR/(AR+2), explicitly NOT the thin-airfoil 2*pi limit which overestimates CL_alpha at AR=6 by ~39% and inflates gust loads.

A GustValidityWarning is emitted when mu_g is outside the Pratt-Walker validity range [3, 200]; RC/UAV with low wing loading routinely fall below 3, so their gust loads may be optimistic (gh-497). Previously this was a server-side log only with no frontend feedback.

Performance KPIs carry an explicit confidence ladder: a TRIMMED operating-point marker ('trimmed') beats a polar-derived context value ('computed') beats the heuristic 1.4*V_s / 1.2*V_s ('estimated'), which is documented as ~15% wrong for high-AR airframes and kept only for cold start.

SM classification (Scholz 4.2): sm < 0.02 error (Phugoid divergent), sm < target warn, sm <= 0.20 ok, sm <= 0.30 warn (heavy nose / trim drag), else error (elevator authority). The 0.30*MAC forward CG limit is a conservative STUB overridden by elevator_authority_service.compute_forward_cg_limit (gh-500); on failure the stub is kept and SM values are stored as None rather than as deceptive stubs.

gh-477 landing field length: V_TD = 1.15*V_S0, s_ground = V_TD^2/(2*g*mu_eff) (mass cancels), L = safety*(15 m flare + s_ground); net_recovery collapses s_ground to 0. mu_eff values come from operational RC/UAV practice, explicitly not from Anderson.

The matching chart imports the Loftin/Roskam constants (_K_TO_50FT 1.66, _K_LDG_50FT 2.73, _K_LDG_HARD 0.5847, _C_TO 1.21) from field_length_service rather than re-declaring them, explicitly to guarantee zero drift.

gh-613 Phase B: _PROFILE_CONSTRAINT_MAP restricts which constraints apply per mission profile (a sailplane is evaluated against the stall constraint only); an unknown or 'custom' profile falls back to all constraints for backward compatibility. The user-controlled profile string is never logged raw - it is mapped through a constant table for Sonar S5145 (log forging).
The stall constraint uses CL_max CLEAN (not the landing-flaps CL_max) per spec: W/S_max = 0.5*rho*V_s_target^2*CL_max_clean.

recompute_assumptions is layered by failure severity: an AeroBuildup failure in the stability/coarse/fine stages aborts and leaves the previous context valid; per-configuration polars each sit in their own try (a takeoff failure must not block the physically independent landing pass) and fall back to a clean clone with provenance='aerobuildup_failed'; a schema/ASB flap-name parity mismatch routes to the no-flap fallback with an explicit 'investigate the converter' warning instead of raising AssertionError on the live path (gh-537).

Deleting an rc_flight_profile that is still assigned to any aircraft returns 409 Conflict; an unassigned aircraft falls back to _default_profile() with source_profile_id=None, which is the signal that lets the cruise speed be replaced by the computed V_md.

mission preset -> design assumption estimate propagation on mission_type change
15-target operating-point sizing sweep with capability gating and flap clipping
two-stage trim: asb.Opti weighted-residual minimisation then a velocity x alpha x beta grid fallback
bounded spawn ProcessPool with BLAS pinning for parallel trim solves (GIL-bound CasADi)
V-n manoeuvre envelope with g_limit and -0.4*g_limit clamps
Pratt-Walker discrete sharp-edged gust envelope with K_g alleviation and validity-range warnings
confidence-ladder KPI derivation (trimmed > computed > estimated > limit)
loading-scenario CG aggregation with toggles, mass/position overrides and adhoc items
stability envelope with a 0.30*MAC stub overridden by elevator-authority physics
landing field length from an energy balance with a per-surface friction table
Loftin/Scholz matching chart with per-profile constraint applicability and RC-additive constraints (WCL, power loading, vertical climb, hand launch)
Reynolds-banded polar re-binning with 1/sqrt(Re) cd0 interpolation and Picard speed refinement

business_rules: One components table for every hardware type; the discriminator is component_type and the per-type contract is DATA (component_types.schema)
12 seeded types are deletable=False; a type referenced by any component cannot be deleted (409)
A type's name and deletable flag are immutable after creation; only label/description/schema may change
Battery voltage is ALWAYS 3.7 V/cell loaded, never 4.2 V peak (a 13 % power inflation)
Motor RPM must use output_kv = kv_rpm_per_volt / (gear_ratio or 1); gear-blind consumers are a bug
eta_prop is J-dependent (Pe from the polar), never a flat 0.65 scalar in the performance model
Torque is derived as P/(2*pi*n), never read from the stored Torque_Nm (3-dp precision loss at low RPM)
Ct is clamped at 0 - the negative windmilling tail is out of scope
Advance-ratio extrapolation beyond the dataset clamps J and emits an explicit warning
The committed snapshot (data/cots/*.json[.gz]) is the durable reimport source; raw vendor files are gitignored and never re-hosted
Reimport skips a row when source_version, source_url, variant and weight presence all match; --force overrides
_upsert_samples replaces ALL samples for a propeller - there is no per-sample diff
A PE0 weight below 1 g is treated as a kg->g error and rejected, never written
propeller_polars.weight_g and components.mass_g are BOTH grams - no conversion; NULL means mass unknown (no 0 fallback)
A user-entered components.mass_g is never clobbered by a reseed
Aero inputs come from assumption_computation_context first (gh-924); every fallback emits a named warning
In the solution space P_top_elec is already battery power: I = P/V_sag, dividing again by the efficiencies double-counts (gh-978)
Motor catalog ratings are SHAFT power, so the comparison uses P_aero/eta_prop, not P_aero
An empty component catalog returns explicit warnings, never a silent empty table (gh-992)
Confidence scales linearly with flight_time/target and is capped at 1.0 - no discontinuity (gh-992)
algorithms: APC PER3 parsing: header-line designation (handles 105x45 -> 10.5x4.5 and variant suffixes), SI columns only, blade count from a trailing -[3-9] token that must not match letter suffixes (M-JK)
Fixed-RPM motor model: n = output_kv * V_bat * throttle; P_elec = min(motor, battery limit); P_shaft = clip(Cp*rho*n^3*D^5, 0, P_elec*eta_motor)
QPROP 3-parameter torque balance: bisect 80x on Q_motor(I) - Q_prop(n) = 0 with I(n) = (V - omega/Kv_si)/Rm, Q_motor = (I-I0)/Kv_si, Q_prop = Cp*rho*n^2*D^5/(2*pi); eta = (V-I*Rm)(I-I0)/(V*I)
Bracketing: rpm_hi = free-run (I->0), rpm_lo = the back-EMF floor set by max_current_a; monotone residual
Linear interpolation of Ct/Cp vs J within the nearest-RPM row group, with clamping + extrapolation warning

Solution space: C_L = 2mg/(rho V^2 S); C_D = cd0 + C_L^2/(pi e AR); P_aero = 0.5 rho V^3 S C_D; E_Wh = P_elec(V_cruise) t/DoD; per cell count I_peak = P_top/V_sag, cap = E/V_nom, C_min = I/(cap) * margin, KV ~ RPM_target/(V_nom * load_rpm_factor)
eta_prop band: every row computed at lo / mid / hi propeller efficiency with the deliberate inversion (high eta -> lower power)
C-rate feasible region sampled as the hyperbola C = I_peak/(cap/1000) over [cap_floor, 4*cap_floor], 40 points
Catalog sweep: motors x batteries cross product, ESC matched by first-fit, flight time = cap_Ah/I * 0.8, confidence = min(t/t_target, 1)
Type-schema validation: required / number range / string / boolean / options with unknown keys tolerated
