entities: CopilotMessageModel (copilot_messages) - aeroplane_id, sort_index, role, content, tool_calls JSON, tool_results JSON, parent_id (dead), created_at
CopilotMessageWrite / CopilotMessageRead / CopilotHistory
CopilotStreamRequest {message, context_hint}
EditOp discriminated union: SetAssumption, SetXsec, SetSegment, AddXsec, RemoveXsec, SetWingParam, ReplaceWingConfig (all mm/degrees)
ToolEntry {schema, impl} + TOOL_REGISTRY (6 tools)
SSE event envelope: token | tool_call | tool_result | done | error
SYSTEM_PROMPT (~270 lines) with the {context_hint} placeholder
COPILOT_API_KEY / COPILOT_BASE_URL / COPILOT_MODEL / COPILOT_EMBEDDING_MODEL (app/core/config.py)
business_rules: Propose, never mutate: every design change goes to a copilot proposal branch; there is deliberately NO adopt tool - only the human adopts in the Versions panel
Exactly ONE open proposal branch per lineage; a second apply_design_edits reuses it so changes accumulate incrementally
Deterministic numbers are computed in the tools, never by the LLM - the induced/parasitic drag split, the neutral-point override and the static-margin recomputation are all Python
One neutral point across the app (gh-924): the stability tool overrides its own x_np with assumption_computation_context.x_np_m
Performance numbers (L/D, v_stall, v_cruise, v_min_sink) must come from a fresh run_analysis, never from diff_proposal_branch / diff_vs_live
Never mix data sources: the snapshot's coarse cd0/e_oswald must not be combined with the polar's CD in one expression
A tool never raises - errors are returned as {'error': ...} so the model can self-correct; apply_edits rejects individual ops with a reason instead of failing the call
Read tools auto-retarget to the open proposal head so the copilot sees its own edits; get_version_tree stays on the live lineage
The API key is never forwarded to the browser: _sanitize_error redacts it and substitutes a category message
AddXsec supports tip-append only; any interior at_index is rejected with a message steering the model to at_index = n_xsecs
Reply in the user's language (German if they write German); UI chrome and code comments stay English
copilot_messages is in EXCLUDED_TABLES - branching an aircraft never copies its conversation
algorithms: Streaming tool-call accumulation: chunks are merged by delta.tool_calls[].index, concatenating id / function.name / function.arguments across the stream
Tool execution off the event loop via asyncio.to_thread, which is exactly what lets _run_analysis call asyncio.run() for the async AeroSandbox path
History replay reconstruction (gh-922): one synthetic role='tool' message per persisted tool_call, matched by tool_call_id
Station<->segment index algebra: n segments => n+1 stations; an interior station writes BOTH seg[i-1].tip_airfoil and seg[i].root_airfoil
Per-wing in-memory WingConfig cache so multiple ops on one wing compose, written once at the end; ReplaceWingConfig writes immediately and evicts

AddXsec tip-append strips tip_type from ALL trailing segments, because create_wing_configuration processes middle segments (tip_type is None) before tip segments and would otherwise reorder the cross-sections
RemoveXsec merges seg[i-1] and seg[i]: lengths added, sweeps added (the comment says weighted average)
Accumulated dihedral recovered from persisted geometry as atan2(dz, dy) between consecutive leading-edge points
Best-glide selection via nanargmax(CL / where(CD>0, CD, nan))
Session hygiene: db.expire_all() after the deferred wing write, db.expunge_all() before discarding a proposal

modules.name: mcp-server
modules.purpose: Expose the service as a Model Context Protocol server for external AI agents: 76 FastMCP tools that re-enter the existing v2 endpoint functions in-process (no HTTP, no routing, no Depends), plus an asset registry that turns binary results into MCP resources and dual public URLs.

functions.name: mcp_tool
functions.returns: decorator - only RECORDS MCPToolSpec(name, description, handler) in TOOL_SPECS and returns the function unchanged; installation happens later in create_mcp_server

functions.name: _call_endpoint
functions.returns: Any - opens `with SessionLocal() as db`, injects db only if the endpoint signature declares it, awaits if awaitable, normalises the result; NEVER COMMITS and Session.__exit__ rolls back, so every write tool relying on get_db()'s commit silently persists nothing

functions.name: _normalize_result
functions.returns: Any - None -> {'status': 'ok'}; JSONResponse -> parsed body; FileResponse -> {file_path, filename, media_type}; image Response -> base64 envelope; else jsonable_encoder

functions.name: create_mcp_server
functions.returns: FastMCP('da3dalus-cad-tools') - installs all 76 TOOL_SPECS via mcp.tool(...) and the two resource templates img://{asset_id} and data://{asset_id}

functions.name: create_mcp_http_app
functions.returns: ASGI app mounted at /mcp by app.main.create_app; its lifespan is nested inside _combined_lifespan

functions.name: register_file_asset
functions.returns: AssetEntry - copies the file to tmp/mcp_assets/external/<uuid4>_<name> when it is not already under tmp/; stores it in the process-local ASSET_REGISTRY under ASSET_REGISTRY_LOCK

functions.name: _asset_payload
functions.returns: dict - resource_uri (img:// | data://), url_from_docker_container (request-derived) and url_for_webui / url (settings.base_url) - the dual-URL answer to agent-vs-browser network views

functions.name: resolve_public_base_url
functions.returns: str - MCP Context request URL, else fastmcp get_http_request(), else settings.base_url; a trailing '/mcp' is stripped from the path prefix

functions.name: read_image_asset / read_data_asset
functions.returns: ResourceResult - NotFoundError on unknown id, on a kind mismatch (img:// against a data entry) and on a vanished file

functions.name: run_mcp_server
functions.returns: None - standalone FastMCP HTTP server hard-coded to 0.0.0.0:8001 path /mcp, ignoring UVICORN_HOST

entities: MCPToolSpec (frozen dataclass) {name, description, handler} + TOOL_SPECS list + MCP_TOOL_NAMES tuple (76)
AssetEntry (frozen dataclass) {asset_id, kind, file_path, mime_type, public_url, filename}
ASSET_REGISTRY dict + ASSET_REGISTRY_LOCK (threading.Lock) - process-local, never evicted
Resource templates img://{asset_id} (image/png) and data://{asset_id} (application/octet-stream)

Reuses the v2 request/response schemas verbatim: OperatingPointSchema, AlphaSweepRequest, StoredOperatingPointCreate, OperatingPointSetSchema, RCFlightProfileCreate/Update, AssumptionWrite, AssumptionSourceSwitch, AeroplaneSettings, CreatorUrlType, ExporterUrlType, AnalysisToolUrlType
business_rules: MCP is a second front door onto the SAME endpoint functions - never a second implementation
The tool's JSON input schema is derived from the handler signature, so the Pydantic parameter types are the contract; the decorator description is the only prose the agent sees
Binary results never travel as tool JSON: they are registered as assets and returned as a resource URI plus two URLs (container view and browser view)
The MCP surface is frozen at the geometry/analysis core - versioning, copilot, components/COTS, construction plans, powertrain and OpenVSP import have no tools
The server is built at import time (mcp = get_mcp() at module level) and mounted at /mcp with its lifespan nested inside the app lifespan

CONFIRMED DEFECT: MCP write tools do not persist - _call_endpoint never commits and the session context manager rolls back on exit; only services that commit themselves (retrim, operating_point_generator, tessellation) take effect
algorithms: Two-stage registration: a decorator collects MCPToolSpec metadata at import time; create_mcp_server installs them onto FastMCP in one pass
Signature-based dependency injection: inspect.signature(endpoint_fn).parameters decides whether to pass db; other Depends parameters must be supplied by hand (settings=get_settings(), request=None)
Return-type normalisation table mapping FastAPI response classes to MCP-friendly JSON
Base-URL resolution chain: MCP Context -> active HTTP request -> settings.base_url, with '/mcp' stripped from the path prefix
Asset fan-out: bytes assets land in tmp/mcp_assets/<kind>/<first-2-hex>/ to avoid one huge directory
dependencies: app.api.v2.endpoints.* (aeroplane.base, aeroplane.wings, aeroplane.fuselages, aeroplane.design_assumptions, aeroanalysis, airfoils, cad, operating_points, flight_profiles)

modules.name: platform-core
modules.purpose: The cross-cutting foundation: FastAPI app composition and lifespan, router wiring, CORS and static mounts, the two Settings classes, the ServiceException hierarchy and its HTTP translation, the SQLAlchemy engine/session with its transaction contract, platform capability probes, the in-process event bus and the debounced background-job tracker.

functions.name: create_app
functions.returns: FastAPI - builds the MCP app first, wires 15 unconditional + up to 5 capability-gated routers, adds wide-open CORS, ensures tmp/, mounts /static /assets /mcp, and serves a custom /docs

functions.name: _combined_lifespan
functions.returns: asynccontextmanager - seeds component types and mission presets (both never-block-on-failure), registers invalidation handlers, binds the event loop and the trim/recompute functions on job_tracker, then nests mcp_app.lifespan; on teardown shuts down job_tracker and both ProcessPoolExecutors

functions.name: service_exception_handler
functions.returns: JSONResponse {'error': {code, message, details}} - 404/422/409/500 by subclass; details passed through jsonable_encoder with a BaseException custom encoder; 4xx logged INFO, 5xx logged exception

functions.name: get_db
functions.returns: Session generator - THE transaction boundary: commit on success, rollback on exception, close in finally; services must never call commit() or begin()

functions.name: _set_sqlite_pragmas
functions.returns: None - PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=30000 on every new SQLite connection, because the assumption recompute holds a write transaction for seconds

functions.name: cad_available / aerosandbox_available
functions.returns: bool - lru_cache(maxsize=1) import probes; a broken install detected once stays broken for the life of the process

functions.name: require_cad / require_aerosandbox
functions.returns: None or HTTPException 503 - FastAPI dependencies gating endpoints on the probes

functions.name: EventBus.publish
functions.returns: None - synchronous in-process fan-out; every handler is wrapped in try/except so a broken subscriber cannot break the publishing request

functions.name: register_handlers
functions.returns: None - subscribes 4 handlers; AssumptionChanged only acts for params in {mass, cg_x} (retrim) and {target_static_margin, mass} (recompute); cg_x/cd0/cl_max are excluded to break a recompute loop

functions.name: mark_ops_dirty
functions.returns: int - bulk UPDATE operating_points SET status='DIRTY' WHERE aircraft_id=? AND status NOT IN ('DIRTY','COMPUTING'); called by seven PUBLISHERS by hand right before event_bus.publish, never by a handler

functions.name: JobTracker._create_task_safe
functions.returns: asyncio.Task | None - uses the running loop when there is one, else call_soon_threadsafe onto the bound main loop with a 2.0 s threading.Event wait; returns None (schedule silently dropped) when no loop is bound or the wait times out

functions.name: JobTracker.schedule_retrim / schedule_recompute_assumptions
functions.returns: None - CREATE the new debounce task first, only then cancel the old one, so a None result never strands a job in DEBOUNCING; retrim also short-circuits while COMPUTING, recompute does not

functions.name: NonFiniteSafeJSONResponse.render
functions.returns: bytes - NaN / +/-Inf (Python and numpy) become null with a WARNING count; null is an honest 'no value', never a fabricated fallback. Applied to exactly ONE router today (aeroanalysis)

functions.name: get_health
functions.returns: HealthResponse {status, version, database} - always HTTP 200 so a load balancer can distinguish 'down' from 'up but degraded'; must never import CadQuery/AeroSandbox

entities: Settings #1 (app/core/config.py): PROJECT_NAME, VERSION='1.0.0', UVICORN_HOST, ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIR, COPILOT_* + module constants REPO_ROOT / AIRFOILS_DIR
Settings #2 (app/settings.py): base_url, openai_api_key, version='0.1.0', low_re_* (13) + _DEFAULT_LOW_RE_GRID / _DEFAULT_MISSION_WEIGHTS
ServiceException / NotFoundError / ValidationError / ValidationDomainError / ConflictError / InternalError
DomainEvent / GeometryChanged(source_model) / AssumptionChanged(parameter_name) + EventBus singleton event_bus
JobStatus enum (DEBOUNCING, COMPUTING, DONE, FAILED), RetrimJob, RecomputeAssumptionsJob, JobTracker singleton job_tracker
HealthResponse {status, version, database}
SQLAlchemy Base (implicit id PK + lowercase __tablename__), engine, SessionLocal
NonFiniteSafeJSONResponse / replace_nonfinite
business_rules: get_db() owns the transaction: commit on success, rollback on exception; services may flush/expire/expunge but never commit or begin
The service starts even where CadQuery/AeroSandbox are unavailable (linux/aarch64): heavy routers are registered behind lru_cached import probes and /health always answers
Startup seeding never blocks startup - seed_default_types (gh#83) and seed_mission_presets (gh-546) log a WARNING and continue on failure
Route order is load-bearing: the versioning router is included before the aeroplane router so /aeroplanes/compare beats /aeroplanes/{id} (gh-914)
Non-finite solver output is rendered as JSON null with a WARNING, never as a fabricated fallback number
CPU-bound work never runs on the event loop: the assumption recompute is wrapped in asyncio.to_thread and owns its own session
Capability-gated endpoints return a clean 503 with an explanatory message rather than an opaque ModuleNotFoundError
All configuration is supposed to flow through the settings layer - SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL, LOG_LEVEL and DISPLAY_CONSTRUCTION_STEP are documented exceptions that use bare os.getenv
algorithms: Import-time capability probing with per-router try/except ImportError, so a missing optional dependency degrades to a 404 instead of a startup crash
Lifespan composition: the app lifespan nests the FastMCP lifespan and guarantees ProcessPoolExecutor teardown in a finally block
Debounce state machine (2.0 s) with create-before-cancel ordering, because task creation can legitimately fail from a worker thread
Cross-thread scheduling via call_soon_threadsafe + threading.Event with a 2 s timeout, returning a real asyncio.Task so the debounce-cancel path still works
Recursive non-finite sanitisation that treats bool before float and matches np.floating explicitly (numpy floats are not float subclasses)
Uniform error envelope with jsonable_encoder(custom_encoder={BaseException: str}) so an exception inside details serialises instead of crashing the handler
SQLite WAL + busy_timeout to let a multi-second write transaction coexist with reads
dependencies: every app.api.v2.endpoints router (15 unconditional + 5 capability-gated + 24 aeroplane sub-routers)

modules.name: frontend-workbench
modules.purpose: The Next.js 16 / React 19 design workbench: one client-side shell with seven tabs (wing & fuselage editor, analysis, components/COTS, mission, powertrain, construction plans, airfoil preview) plus a docked AI copilot strip, a metrics dashboard and a version-graph overlay - all driven by SWR hooks that call the FastAPI v2 API directly from the browser. ~47,700 LOC.

functions.name: RootLayout
functions.returns: JSX - the only meaningful SERVER component: loads Geist / Geist_Mono / JetBrains_Mono via next/font/google, sets metadata and the font CSS variables; everything below /workbench is 'use client'

functions.name: WorkbenchLayout / WorkbenchInner
functions.returns: JSX - Suspense > AeroplaneProvider > UnsavedChangesProvider wrapping Header, WorkbenchImportWarningBanner, the active tab, VersionGraphOverlay (key=rootId), MetricsDashboardContainer (gh-881), CopilotStrip, UnsavedChangesModal and AeroplanePickerHost

functions.name: fetcher / putJson
functions.returns: Promise<T> - GET/PUT against API_BASE = NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:8001'; throws a PLAIN Error('<status> <text>: <body>'). This is the fetcher every SWR hook uses

functions.name: fetchAPI / api.get|post|put|delete
functions.returns: Promise<T> - the richer client: Content-Type header, 204 -> undefined, throws a typed ApiError(status, message, details). NOT used by the SWR hooks, so two error shapes coexist

functions.name: parseSseStream
functions.returns: AsyncIterable<SseEvent> - hand-written SSE parser because EventSource only supports GET and both backend streams are POST; buffers the trailing incomplete record across chunks, JSON with raw-string fallback

functions.name: AeroplaneProvider / useAeroplaneContext
functions.returns: context {aeroplaneId, hydrated, selectedWing, selectedXsecIndex, selectedFuselage, selectedFuselageXsecIndex, treeMode, pickerOpen, lastImportWarnings, ...setters} - ?aeroplane=<uuid> is the source of truth, mirrored to localStorage['da3dalus_aeroplane_id']

functions.name: useCopilot
functions.returns: {history, sendMessage, streamingText, toolActivity, errorMessage} - SWR for GET /copilot-history, POST /copilot/stream consumed via parseSseStream, mutate() on 'done'; TOOL_LABEL_MAP covers only 3 of the 6 copilot tools

functions.name: useTessellation / invalidateTessellationCache
functions.returns: {data, isTessellating, progress, error} - module-level Map keyed `${aeroplaneId}/${wingName}`, validated against the aeroplane's updated_at; unbounded, no eviction policy

functions.name: CadViewer
functions.returns: JSX - STATIC css import ('three-cad-viewer/css', l.6) + RUNTIME dynamic import (await import('three-cad-viewer'), l.90). The asymmetry is deliberate and fragile - never change without real browser testing

functions.name: useLineageTree / useVersionActions
functions.returns: {tree, mutate} and {snapshot, branch, adopt, restore, discard} - every mutation revalidates BOTH the lineage tree and the aeroplanes list; versioning routes take the integer PK while the rest of the app uses UUIDs

entities: AeroplaneContextValue - aeroplaneId (uuid), hydrated, selectedWing, selectedXsecIndex, selectedFuselage, selectedFuselageXsecIndex, treeMode ('wingconfig' | 'asb' | 'fuselage'), pickerOpen, lastImportWarnings
SseEvent<T> {event, data} (lib/sseStream.ts)
ApiError {status, message, details} (lib/api.ts only)
types/versioning.ts - TreeOut, VersionNode, BranchOut, BranchRequest, SnapshotRequest, CompareOut (the ONLY shared backend mirror)
types/versionGraph.ts - layout types for lib/versionGraphLayout.ts
CopilotMessageRead / CopilotHistory + TokenEvent / ToolCallEvent / DoneEvent / ErrorEvent (hand-mirrored inside useCopilot.ts)
Design tokens in app/globals.css @theme inline - background #111111, primary #FF8400, card #1A1A1A, destructive #E5484D, success #30A46C, dark-only
localStorage keys: da3dalus_aeroplane_id + per-feature UI state (CopilotStrip, import banners, StabilityOverlay, versionGraphViewState)
business_rules: The workbench is a client-side SPA inside the App Router: no route handlers, no server actions, no server-side fetching - every call is a direct cross-origin browser fetch, which is why the backend runs allow_origins=['*']
?aeroplane=<uuid> in the URL is the source of truth for the selected aircraft; localStorage is only the restore fallback
treeMode exposes the backend unit duality to the user: 'wingconfig' = millimetre segments, 'asb' = metre cross-sections, 'fuselage' = fuselage stations
A null SWR key disables the request - the universal 'nothing selected yet' guard across all 48 hooks
Plotly is ALWAYS lazily imported inside an effect (1.5 MB) and purged on unmount; react-plotly.js is never used
three is aliased to a single resolved path in both webpack and turbopack so the app and three-cad-viewer share one three.js instance
The copilot strip and the metrics dashboard are docked on EVERY tab; the version graph is a full-screen overlay keyed by rootId
Layering is machine-enforced: components/hooks must never import from app/ (error), hooks/lib should not import components (warn), no cycles (error)
Frontend tests require Node 22 - Node >= 24 breaks jsdom localStorage with spurious failures
CI gates are tsc --noEmit + eslint + vitest + dependency-cruiser; tsc catches what the others miss
UI text is English only
algorithms: SWR key convention: build the path string or null, then rename the result ({tree, wing, ...}) rather than exposing raw `data`
Cross-hook cache invalidation via useSWRConfig().mutate(key) after a write
Hand-written SSE record parser with a cross-chunk buffer, event/data line splitting and JSON-with-raw-fallback decoding
Tessellation memoisation keyed by aeroplaneId+wingName and validated against the aeroplane's updated_at timestamp before reuse
Version graph layout in lib/versionGraphLayout.ts with pan/zoom persisted through lib/versionGraphViewState.ts
Geometry diffing in lib/geometryDiff.ts and provenance badge derivation in lib/versionProvenance.ts (human vs ai vs copilot)
Tailwind v4 @theme inline design tokens with an explicit @source over streamdown/dist so the copilot markdown classes survive purging
dependencies: plotly.js-gl3d-dist-min 3.5 (all charts; react-plotly.js declared but unused)
streamdown + remark-math + remark-breaks + rehype-katex + katex (copilot markdown)
the FastAPI v2 REST API at NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL (default http://localhost:8001) - never /mcp
